geometry.note: OpenStreetMap outline alone; no official figure checks it. Its long axis (55.6 m) is shorter than the overall setup length stated by KATRIN ('about 70 m'; 'exceeds 70 meters'), so the outline is the experiment's footprint beside the Tritium Laboratory, not the whole beamline.
geometry.quote: The overall length of the setup is about 70 m

method: OpenStreetMap way 394890935, name 'Karlsruhe-Tritium-Neutrino-Experiment', short_name KATRIN (man_made=observatory, observatory:type=neutrino, indoor=yes, start_date=2018-06-11), a 13-node outline used verbatim. The long sides run at bearings of 15.8-16.1 degrees from north. Its centroid lies about 10 m from the coordinate the German Wikipedia article gives for KATRIN (49.095717 N, 8.436117 E; rank 12, corroboration only).
name: KATRIN experiment outline (spectrometer hall and beamline, OpenStreetMap)
notes: The outline abuts the east end of Tritium Laboratory building 452 and overlaps OSM building 460; the KATRIN paper places the WGTS source cryostat in the TLK hall, so the source and part of the transport section lie inside the TLK buildings, outside this outline.

What the outline depicts (spectrometer hall versus beamline footprint) is the OSM mapper's choice; no fetched source states the hall's dimensions or building number, so it is typed experimental_area rather than hall.

summary.plain: The ground outline of the KATRIN neutrino-mass experiment at KIT Campus North as mapped in OpenStreetMap: a narrow strip about 56 metres long and 12 to 16 metres wide, running roughly north-north-east beside the Tritium Laboratory.
